title: Shadows
coreIdea: Make the shadow the primary subject or an equal partner to the object that casts it.
whyItMatters: Shadows are pure graphic form and can function as secondary figures. Seeing them as content rather than byproduct changes how you use light.
shootingBrief: Hard light conditions. Minimum 8 frames where the shadow is essential. Experiment with including and excluding the casting object. Volume 40–70.
technicalFocus: Settings: Expose for highlights if you want deep graphic black shadows.
Focusing: On the shadow plane or casting object depending on which is primary.
Stance: Position relative to light direction is critical.
Light: Hard, directional light only. Soft light kills the exercise.
failureModes: Including too much of the casting object so shadow becomes secondary.
Busy ground that breaks the shadow shape.

goodVsExcellent.excellent: The shadow is more interesting or more complete than the object, or the two form a single graphic idea.

title: Reflections
coreIdea: Use reflective surfaces to create layered or doubled realities and deliberately control the mix of reflection and direct view.
whyItMatters: Reflections multiply information in a single frame and introduce controlled ambiguity. Tiny changes in angle completely rewrite the content.
shootingBrief: Windows, puddles, polished metal, mirrors. Decide whether reflection, reflected subject, or interaction is primary. Minimum 6 intentional frames. Volume 40–70.
technicalFocus: Settings: Watch exposure — reflective surfaces trick meters.
Focusing: On the reflection plane or key subject within it.
Stance: Tiny angle and height changes rewrite what is reflected. Work slowly.
Control or eliminate your own reflection unless deliberate.
failureModes: Muddy mix of reflection and reality with no hierarchy.

goodVsExcellent.excellent: Reflection and direct view create genuine tension or new meaning neither has alone.

title: Doubles
coreIdea: Find or wait for visual pairs — similar shapes, postures, gestures, or forms that echo each other inside the frame.
whyItMatters: Visual rhyme creates instant structure and often humor or tension. Trains coincidence recognition and holding a frame open for the second element.
shootingBrief: Pairs of people, person + object, repeated gestures, matching forms. Minimum 6 clear doubles. Volume 40–70. Timing is usually critical.
technicalFocus: Settings: Shutter fast enough for gesture.
Focusing: On the plane of the critical pair.
Stance: Position so both elements sit in clear relationship. Longer end helps compress.

goodVsExcellent.excellent: The echo is precise and the rest of the frame supports the relationship without distraction.

title: Empty
coreIdea: Photograph urban emptiness and quiet so that absence itself becomes the subject.
whyItMatters: Most street photographers only feel competent when people are present. Empty frames force reliance on light, geometry, and atmosphere.
shootingBrief: Early morning streets, closed shops, vacant lots, quiet alleys, deserted platforms. Minimum 6 frames that convey emptiness or solitude. Volume 30–50.
technicalFocus: Settings: Can use lower shutter if the scene is static.
Focusing: On the strongest geometric or light plane.
Stance: Precise framing; edges matter more when content is sparse.
Light: Directional light or interesting sky is often essential.

goodVsExcellent.excellent: Emptiness has mood, the frame feels complete, and the picture would be weaker with a person added.

title: Objects
coreIdea: Treat ordinary urban objects as the primary subject with the same seriousness you give people.
whyItMatters: Objects carry atmosphere, social information, humor, and graphic power. Expands subject range and improves still-life seeing on the street.
shootingBrief: Chairs, signs, barriers, discarded items, street furniture. Minimum 8 frames where an object is clearly the subject. Volume 40–60. Context and light matter.
technicalFocus: Settings: f/4–8 depending on desired depth.
Stance: Get closer when it strengthens form. Watch backgrounds.
Light: Side light or hard light reveals texture and volume.

goodVsExcellent.excellent: The object feels charged — lonely, funny, graphic, or socially revealing.
